title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-06-05
lineage: MSR> CASS> DAT> CDR> EAC> FLAC and Audience (shnid:109847) Lineage: Source #1: Dire Wolf through New Speedway - unknown gen aud cassette; Source #2: Cold Rain through Mama Tried - unknown gen aud cassette; Source #3: Cryptical through Casey -  unknown gen aud cassette
source: Matrix from Soundboard (shnid:28653) (except where patched with low gen AUD as noted)

ai_review.summary: Matrix recording with clear acoustic vocals and a stellar set featuring an iconic I Know You Rider and standout Easy Wind, It’s A Man’s World, and Other One > Attics
ai_review.review: The tape captures a beautifully clear acoustic portion—Garcia’s voice crystal‑clear and Weir’s sweet harmonies—followed by electric sets that deadheads hail as peak performances of the summer ’70 run. Highlights include a top‑five acoustic rendition of “I Know You Rider,” a gorgeous “Black Peter,” and an electrifying “Easy Wind/It’s A Man’s World” stretch, all presented on a solid matrix mix that improves after “Dire Wolf.”

ai_rating.rationale: Reviews overwhelmingly praise the musical performance and highlight several standout songs; recording quality is noted as clear and pleasant, yielding a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Garcia’s voice and Weir’s vocals are described as crystal‑clear; sound improves after “Dire Wolf,” giving a crisp acoustic feel. No major dropouts noted, though one reviewer missed Phil’s backing vocals.

standout_songs: That's It For The Other One > Attics
show_quality.setlist_flow: Mellow, high‑quality acoustic set leads into varied electric sets; reviewers note the run’s overall energy and celebrate its fifth‑anniversary vibe.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's voice is praised as crystal clear; noted for singing a different word with Bob on “I Know You Rider.”
band_member_comments.Phil: No backing vocals heard on acoustic set, but no negative comments about his playing.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocal harmonies described as sweet; shares the humorous lyric swap with Jerry.
